tyler: heads-up — just saw a weird token-id drift when converting a sentencepiece HF model to our BPE pipeline. seems tied to non-breaking-space (U+00A0) and zero-width-joiner (U+200D) handling.

sara: ugh. repro steps? model name? :thinking:

tyler: model is community/latin-spm-chat-1.0. steps: load spm tokenizer + export vocab -> run our spm_to_bpe script -> rebuild merges. after conversion, special tokens indexes are off by one in the model config. quick snip: ```python
# simplified
sp = SentencePieceProcessor(model_file='spm.model')
sp_vocab = [sp.id_to_piece(i) for i in range(sp.get_piece_size())]
# our converter collapses \u00A0 to ' ' and strips \u200D in some rules
```

alex: did you check for invisible chars in the vocab file? NBSP vs regular space will change token strings and then sort order if you regenerate the vocab file (we sort by piece string in the converter). that will permute token ids.

tyler: exact issue — converters normalized NBSP->space before merge grouping, so tokens like '\u00A0hello' became ' hello' and merged with existing ' hello' entries. result: duplicates removed and id assignments shifted.

jamie: also worth noting our chat template injection expects <|system|> to be at a fixed id (we historically appended it). if the HF tokenizer already had an extra invisible token earlier in the list, appending changes the final id. that can silently break role parsing and eval prompts.

ciara: short-term mitigation: explicit mapping step that preserves raw piece strings when generating the new vocab order. i.e., do NOT normalize NBSP/ZWJ until after id mapping is locked. we can add a config flag `preserve_whitespace_codepoints: true`.

tyler: logged a failing eval on the reasoning benchmark — outputs were off-format after conversion. correlates with token id mismatch across system messages.

alex: can you paste a diff of first 20 tokens pre/post?

tyler: sure — pre/post sample (ids trimmed):
```
# pre (spm ids -> pieces)
0: <pad>
1: <unk>
2: \u00A0hello
3: world
4: <|system|>

# post (after our convert)
0: <pad>
1: <unk>
2:  hello  # NBSP normalized -> regular space piece merged
3: world
4: <|system|>  # id bumped but now points to different raw piece in model weights
```

sara: that explains the model->tokenizer mismatch at runtime. weights expect token id 4 to be the system token, but tokenizer emits id 4 for something else.

ciara: long-term fix: make converter emit a `token_map.json` that explicitly maps old_id->new_id and keep a small compatibility layer in Redwood runtime that can remap ids for pinned model versions during load. should be reversible and logged during onboarding.

jamie: also add a test that runs a tiny prompt including NBSP and ZWJ characters through tokenizer->detokenizer roundtrip; flag if any codepoint lost.

tyler: created PR with minimal patch: preserve rare whitespace codepoints while computing ordering + write token_map. tests added. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/convert/pull/342 :rocket:

redwood-bot: CI status — conversion-tests: failed for python3.9 on ubuntu-20.04 (flake8 error). see https://ci.internal/342

sara: will fix lint; +1 to token_map feature. can we also add a small eval run in onboarding that verifies system token ID matches model config before marking model `ready`?

ciara: yes, add gating check in onboarding script. if mismatch, auto-fail and attach token_map suggestion.

alex: thanks. this whole NBSP/ZWJ gotcha has bitten multiple teams before. can we add a one-liner in docs (devex) and a pointer in the model-checklist?

jamie: assigning follow-ups: tyler -> merge converter fix & tests; sara -> lint; ciara -> onboarding gate + runtime remap; alex -> docs blurb.

tyler: on it. will ping once CI green. :thumbsup:
